answer: To achieve Sybil resistance, an economy of AI agents deploys a graph-based transitive trust protocol anchored by verifiable work or staked capital. Trust scores propagate from root identities along a cryptographically signed vine of peer attestations, decaying exponentially over path distance. When a malicious entity generates a gale of fake agent identities, the trust ripple fails to cross bottlenecks, isolating the Sybil cluster and forcing the attacker to incur exorbitant capital costs to acquire valid root attestations.
